title: Feature Request: Allow Permanent Read Access to External Folders in Copilot Chat
body:
## Problem

When using Copilot Chat's agent mode, tools like `read_file`, `grep_search`, `file_search`, and `semantic_search` are restricted to files within the current workspace. To read files from folders outside the workspace, users must either:

- Have the file open in an editor tab (session-based, not persistent)
- Use a multi-root workspace (requires restructuring the workspace)
- Approve access each time when prompted

This limitation significantly impacts productivity when referencing related repositories.

## Inconsistent Security Model

There's a notable inconsistency in the current approach:

- **Terminal access is unrestricted**: The agent can run `Get-Content`, `cat`, `type`, or any file-reading command via `run_in_terminal` without special approval, reading any file on the system
- **`read_file` tool blocks external files**: Requires explicit approval or fails entirely for files outside the workspace

This creates a confusing UX where the agent could simply use terminal commands to bypass the restriction, making the `read_file` limitation feel arbitrary rather than providing real security.

## Proposed Solution

Add a new setting, such as `chat.additionalReadAccessFolders`, that allows users to specify folders outside the workspace that Copilot Chat read-only tools can access permanently.

### Suggested Behavior

- **Read-only access**: Allow `read_file`, `grep_search`, `file_search`, and `semantic_search` on these folders (edit tools remain workspace-restricted)
- **Workspace and global setting**: This should be available as both a workspace-level setting (for project-specific configuration) and a global user setting (for shared folders across all workspaces)
- **Glob support**: Allow patterns like `/mnt/repos/*` to include multiple sibling repos
- **Variable expansion**: Support `${workspaceFolder}`, etc.
- **Consistent with terminal**: If the terminal can already read these paths freely, the read tools should be able to as well

## Use Cases

- **Cross-repository context**: Reading types/contracts from a sibling API repository
- **Documentation reference**: Accessing centralized docs folder without adding it to workspace
- **Pattern discovery**: Searching for implementations across related projects
- **Code comparison**: Understanding how similar problems were solved in other repositories

## Additional Context

The current implementation in `toolUtils.ts` checks `workspaceService.getWorkspaceFolder()`. Since terminal commands already have unrestricted file system access, extending read-only trust to file tools for user-configured folders would provide a more consistent and efficient experience without increasing security risk.

---
cc @roblourens @hediet

body:
It has been nearly three years since the release of the Dark/Light Modern themes, and the developer tools landscape has evolved significantly. With the rise of AI adoption and a rapidly changing ecosystem, it is the perfect time to refresh the UI—helping VS Code stand out while delivering an improved developer experience.

### The Goal: Focus

The core philosophy behind these new themes is simple: **Focus**.
We believe a cleaner environment helps developers maintain their flow state for longer. To achieve this, we are experimenting with several key design pillars:

- **Reduced Palette**: Minimizing visual noise by stripping away unnecessary colors.
- **Strategic Accents**: Using accent colors sparingly to highlight important actions only when relevant.
- **Layered UI**: distinct visual separation between three key areas:
    - Workbench (Editor area)
    - Tools (Chat, Terminal, Explorer)
    - Actions (Quick Pick, Notifications, Menus)

- Depth & Lightness: Utilizing transparency, blur, and shadows to maintain visual context without clutter.


### Try it Out

We have a first WIP iteration of these themes - `VS Code Dark` and `VS Code Light` - available starting in v1.109, and will be continually updating them in Insiders. We welcome your feedback!

Please open issues for bugs or suggestions and attach the 2026-themes label.

title: MCP Server `gallery` Field Not Saved During Protocol Installation
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->

<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->


## Description

When installing an MCP server via the `vscode:mcp/install` protocol URL, the `gallery` field is incorrectly removed from the server configuration and not saved to `mcp.json`. This prevents VS Code from:
- Fetching server metadata from the registry
- Displaying proper server information
- Checking for updates
- Managing server enablement based on gallery status

## Root Cause

In `src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/browser/mcpWorkbenchService.ts` at line 675, the `handleMcpInstallUri` method destructures the `gallery` field out of the configuration object but never uses it:

```typescript
const { name, inputs, gallery, ...config } = parsed;
//                      ^^^^^^^ extracted but never used
```

This removes `gallery` from the `config` object that gets passed to the installation process, so it's never written to `mcp.json`.

## Expected Behavior

The `gallery` field should be preserved in the MCP server configuration since it's a valid field defined in `IMcpServerConfiguration` interface (`src/vs/platform/mcp/common/mcpPlatformTypes.ts` line 32):

```typescript
export interface ICommonMcpServerConfiguration {
    readonly type: McpServerType;
    readonly version?: string;
    readonly gallery?: boolean | string;  // Valid configuration field
}
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open VS Code
2. Create a protocol URL with a `gallery` field:
   ```
   vscode:mcp/install?%7B%22name%22%3A%22test-server%22%2C%22url%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fmcp%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22http%22%2C%22gallery%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fregistry%2Fservers%2Ftest%2Flatest%22%7D
   ```
   
   Decoded JSON:
   ```json
   {
     "name": "test-server",
     "url": "https://example.com/mcp",
     "type": "http",
     "gallery": "https://example.com/registry/servers/test/latest"
   }
   ```

3. Click the protocol URL or navigate to it in a browser
4. VS Code opens and processes the installation
5. Open `mcp.json` file (location varies by OS):
   - **macOS**: `~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/mcp.json`
   - **Windows**: `%APPDATA%\Code\User\mcp.json`
   - **Linux**: `~/.config/Code/User/mcp.json`

## Actual Result

The `gallery` field is missing from the saved configuration:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "test-server": {
      "url": "https://example.com/mcp",
      "type": "http"
    }
  }
}
```

## Expected Result

The `gallery` field should be preserved:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "test-server": {
      "url": "https://example.com/mcp",
      "type": "http",
      "gallery": "https://example.com/registry/servers/test/latest"
    }
  }
}
```

## Proposed Fix

Remove `gallery` from the destructuring assignment so it remains in the `config` object:

**Current (buggy) code:**
```typescript
const { name, inputs, gallery, ...config } = parsed;
```

**Fixed code:**
```typescript
const { name, inputs, ...config } = parsed;
```

This allows the `gallery` field to remain in the `config` object and be properly saved to `mcp.json`.

## Impact

This bug affects any MCP server installation that uses the protocol handler with a `gallery` URL, preventing VS Code from properly managing gallery-registered servers and accessing their metadata.

## Version Information

- VS Code Version: [Your version]
- OS: [Your OS]
- MCP Feature: Enabled

## Additional Context

The `gallery` field is documented as a valid configuration option and is used throughout the codebase to determine server enablement state (see `getEnablementStatus` method in the same file) and sync with gallery metadata.

title: MCP: Cannot authenticate to multiple Atlassian sites simultaneously - OAuth credentials shared across MCP server configurations
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

**Summary:**
When configuring multiple Atlassian MCP servers pointing to different Atlassian Cloud sites (e.g., site-a.atlassian.net and site-b.atlassian.net), VS Code only retains authentication for one site. The OAuth credential appears to be keyed by the OAuth client ID and/or MCP auth provider identity derived only from the server URL origin, causing all Atlassian MCP connections to share a single token.

**Steps to Reproduce:**
1. Configure two Atlassian MCP servers in `mcp.json` with different names (and different query params to differentiate URLs).
   - Example: `https://mcp.atlassian.com/?site=a` and `https://mcp.atlassian.com/?site=b`
2. Authenticate the first connection — prompted with fresh OAuth flow, select `site-a.atlassian.net`.
3. Authenticate the second connection — prompted to reuse "MCP" credential or "Sign in to another account".
4. Select "Sign in to another account" and authenticate to `site-b.atlassian.net`.
5. Call `getAccessibleAtlassianResources` on both MCP servers.

**Expected Result:**
- Site A connection returns `site-a.atlassian.net`.
- Site B connection returns `site-b.atlassian.net`.

**Actual Result:**
- Both connections return the same site (whichever was authenticated last).
- The second authentication overwrites the first.

**Investigation Notes:**
- Credentials are stored in `~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb`.
- The `dynamicAuthProviders` table entry shows e.g.:
  ```json
  {
    "providerId": "https://mcp.atlassian.com/",
    ...
  }
  ```
- The `providerId` appears to be derived from the URL **origin only**, stripping query parameters.
  This means multiple MCP servers with the same origin but different query params (e.g. `?site=a` vs `?site=b`) resolve to the same `providerId` and therefore share credentials.
- The key uses `https://mcp.atlassian.com/` (without query params) and a shared `clientId`, so all Atlassian MCP servers resolve to the same credential regardless of the configured URL or server name.

**Suggested Fix:**
Include the full configured URL (including query params) **or at minimum the MCP server name from `mcp.json`** when generating the `providerId` / credential key, allowing per-server credential isolation (multiple OAuth tokens per MCP server configuration).

**Workaround:**
Use separate VS Code profiles for each Atlassian site.

**Environment:**
- VS Code: 1.108.2
- GitHub Copilot extension: 1.388.0
- GitHub Copilot Chat extension: 0.36.2
- OS: macOS

title: Elevate AI CLI Terminal Profiles for Enhanced Discoverability
body:
## Summary
Based on a Slack conversation, visibility for Copilot CLI (and future AI CLIs like Claude Agent) within the VS Code terminal dropdown is currently low, limiting growth experiments.

## Proposed Feature
- Explore ways to thoughtfully elevate Copilot CLI in the terminal UI so it's not buried between other profiles (e.g., Azure Cloud Shell, JS Debug Terminal).
- Alternatives suggested:
  - Add a Copilot icon where the 'activate/deactivate' Python button appears. (Currently hidden by default via `python-envs.terminal.showActivateButton`.) This could increase discoverability but may risk clutter as more extensions add buttons.
  - Create a new group in the terminal dropdown:
    ```
    - New Terminal*
    ----
    - New Copilot CLI
    - New Claude Agent
    ----
    - profile
    - profile 2
    ```
    This would give AI CLIs their own section, making them easier to find and experiment with.

## Discussion Points
- Is a dedicated icon in the terminal area scalable if more AI CLIs/agents are added?
- Would grouping AI CLIs in the dropdown improve discoverability and maintain a clean UI?
- What are the possible risks with clutter or inconsistency in the terminal interface if multiple extensions contribute their own UI elements?

## Feedback
This suggestion aims to balance discoverability, growth experimentation, and UI scalability. Input from the team on the best approach would be valuable.

The new context window usage indicator in the chat input (as described in the "Monitor context window usage" section of the [docs](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/chat/copilot-chat-context#_monitor-context-window-usage)) is a useful idea.

title: Add agent identifier to Copilot Chat hook parameters
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

### Feature Description

When working with the Copilot Chat hooks system (e.g., `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`), extension developers often need to approve or reject actions based on the context of which agent is executing a command. Currently, the parameters passed to hooks include fields like `timestamp`, `cwd`, `sessionId`, `hookEventName`, `toolName`, `toolInput`, etc., but there is no way to identify which agent initiated the event.

### Problem

Some workflows require making approval decisions depending on the identity of the agent. For example, an organization may want to automatically approve commands by some agents, but require stricter approval for others. Since the agent identifier is not provided to hook invocations, this scenario is currently not possible.

### Proposed Solution

Add an explicit `agentId` or `agentName` property to the parameter object passed to Copilot Chat hooks, so that consumers can implement agent-specific logic in their hooks or middleware (e.g., allow, reject, or customize actions).

#### Example
```js
// Example of desired hook parameter
{
  agentId: "copilot-xyz",
  agentName: "TeamCopilot",
  // ...existing parameters (timestamp, cwd, sessionId, etc.)
}
```

This addition would allow more flexible policies and better extension of Copilot Chat in multi-agent scenarios.

### Additional Context

This is especially important for environments where multiple agents or custom agents are used and different levels of trust/control are needed.

title: Allow runSubagent tool to specify a language model
body:
## Problem

When the LLM invokes the `runSubagent` built-in tool, the subagent always inherits the parent agent's model (or the custom agent's configured model). There is no way for the LLM to explicitly choose a different model for a subagent invocation, even when the user asks for it (e.g. "use Claude to research this").

Why:
- Multi-model consensus-based review, multiple models running in different subagents; has a growing fanbase
- Picking a faster model for quick research tasks

## Proposal

Add an optional `model` parameter to the `runSubagent` tool schema that accepts a qualified model name in `"Model Name (Vendor)"` format. The schema should dynamically enumerate available agent-mode-suitable models so the LLM knows which values are valid.

### Model resolution priority
1. **Explicit `model` parameter** — if provided and resolved
2. **Agent-configured model** — from the custom agent's `.agent.md` file

title: Adopt GitHub Issue Forms with automatic area labeling for incoming issues
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->


## Summary

This proposal suggests migrating the current Markdown-based issue templates to GitHub Issue Forms, combined with automatic labeling based on user-selected fields. The goal is to reduce the volume of incomplete issues entering the "needs more info" cycle and to remove the manual step of applying area labels during initial triaging.

## Motivation

The current issue templates are free-form Markdown, which allows users to omit critical information such as the product version, operating system, or steps to reproduce. As a result, many issues enter the `needs more info` state and are eventually closed automatically after seven days without resolution. The annual cleanup of December 2025 reported a reduction of nearly 6,000 open issues, which gives an idea of the magnitude of the problem.

While VS Code already has sophisticated automation (the ML classifier running every 30 minutes, the Needs More Info Closer bot, the Feature Request Handler), the initial classification and the completeness of incoming data depend on the user voluntarily providing them.

## Proposed Solution

### 1. Structured Issue Forms by issue type

Define three differentiated YAML templates for:
- Bug reports
- Feature requests  
- Performance issues

Each form would explicitly require the relevant fields (version, OS, affected product area, reproduction steps, logs), with closed dropdown lists for categorical fields like product area (`debug`, `editor`, `terminal`, `extensions`, etc.).

### 2. Automatic area labeling

Configure an existing GitHub Action like [`actions/labeler`](https://github.com/actions/labeler) to apply labels based on the value selected in the "product area" field. This would remove the manual triaging step that maintainers currently perform during the first pass on a new issue.

### 3. "I searched for similar issues" checkbox

Before form submission, include a mandatory checkbox that confirms "I have searched for similar issues", accompanied by a prefabricated link that runs a search in the repository using the terms from the title entered by the author. This does not eliminate duplicates but introduces a minimal barrier that may help reduce their frequency.

## Why this is feasible

The proposal does not introduce experimental technology: GitHub Issue Forms and `actions/labeler` are standard GitHub features, already used by comparable projects such as `golang/go`, `rust-lang/rust`, and `nodejs/node`. No additional infrastructure is required.

## Suggested success metrics

- Percentage of issues that go through the `needs more info` state (target: reduce by half).
- Median time between issue opening and the application of its first area label (target: from hours to seconds).
- Proportion of issues opened that are closed as duplicates within the next 30 days, as an indirect proxy for the effect of the search-previously checkbox.

## Context

This proposal was developed as part of an academic analysis of VS Code's open source engineering practices, focused on the automation gaps observed in the current triaging workflow.

title: vscode.lm — Add model visibility (hide/show) APIs
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
**Problem Statement**
VS Code's chat model picker (Settings gear → "Manage Models") provides a UI to toggle the visibility of individual models and entire provider groups. Users can show or hide models from the picker. However, there is no extension API to read or write this visibility state programmatically.

The internal ILanguageModelsService already has full support for model visibility:


Extensions like BYOK/wallet dashboard providers, model management tools, and workspace onboarding assistants need these same capabilities to offer a good experience.

**Proposed API**
Add the following to the `vscode.lm` namespace in `vscode.d.ts`:


Use Cases

- BYOK provider extensions — When a user configures a new BYOK provider (e.g., via a wizard), the extension could initially hide lower-tier models so the picker isn't cluttered, giving the user a curated starting set.

- Workspace onboarding — A .code-workspace or devcontainer setup could programmatically configure which models are visible for a team, ensuring consistency (e.g., hide deprecated models, show only approved ones).

- Custom model management UIs — Extensions that provide alternative model management panels can read the current visibility state to display accurate toggle states, and can write back changes so the built-in picker stays in sync.

- Diagnostics/telemetry — Extension authors can inspect which models users have hidden to better understand adoption patterns and surface relevant guidance.

**Prior Art**
The internal ILanguageModelsService already implements all of these methods. The model visibility state is persisted in VS Code's profile storage (state.vscdb under key "chatModelVisibility") as:

``` ts
export namespace lm {

    // ... existing APIs ...

    /**
     * An event that fires when any model or group visibility state changes
     * (e.g., when a user toggles "Show/Hide" in the Manage Models UI, or
     * when {@link lm.setModelHidden} or {@link lm.setGroupHidden} is called).
     */
    export const onDidChangeModelVisibility: Event<void>;

    /**
     * Returns whether the given model is hidden from the chat model picker.
     *
     * @param modelIdentifier A model identifier string, e.g. `"copilot/gpt-4o"`.
     *   Obtainable from {@link LanguageModelChat.id} when prefixed with the vendor,
     *   or from the result of {@link selectChatModels}.
     */
    export function isModelHidden(modelIdentifier: string): boolean;

    /**
     * Returns whether every model in the given (vendor, groupName) bucket
     * is hidden from the chat model picker.
     *
     * @param vendor The vendor identifier, e.g. `"openai"` or `"copilot"`.
     * @param groupName The configured group name for that vendor.
     */
    export function isGroupHidden(vendor: string, groupName: string): boolean;

    /**
     * Hide or show a single model in the chat model picker.
     *
     * Hidden models are not removed — they remain usable via
     * {@link selectChatModels} and can still be sent requests. Hiding only
     * removes them from the user-facing picker UI.
     *
     * @param modelIdentifier A model identifier string.
     * @param hidden `true` to hide the model, `false` to show it.
     */
    export function setModelHidden(modelIdentifier: string, hidden: boolean): void;

    /**
     * Hide or show every model in a (vendor, groupName) bucket.
     *
     * This is a convenience that operates on all resolved models belonging
     * to the given vendor + group combination at the time of the call.
     * Models resolved later for the same bucket are NOT automatically hidden.
     *
     * @param vendor The vendor identifier.
     * @param groupName The configured group name for that vendor.
     * @param hidden `true` to hide, `false` to show.
     */
    export function setGroupHidden(vendor: string, groupName: string, hidden: boolean): void;

    /**
     * Returns the list of model identifiers that are currently hidden.
     *
     * This can be used to persist or synchronize visibility preferences
     * across machines, or to build custom model management UIs that stay
     * in sync with the built-in picker state.
     */
    export function getHiddenModelIds(): string[];
}
```

The proposed API would simply expose a subset of this existing internal interface through the vscode.lm namespace, with no new storage or behavior — just a bridge from the extension host to the existing main-thread service.

**Non-Goals**
This proposal does not add the ability to hide models from vscode.lm.selectChatModels() — hidden models remain selectable and fully functional. The toggle only affects the user-facing model picker UI.
This proposal does not expose the raw IStorageService or allow extensions to read/write arbitrary storage keys.

title: Security: minimumReleaseAge setting for mitigating supply chain attacks on extensions
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

In the last years, supply chain attacks have increased dramatically. A few examples in the VS Code extension ecosystem:

- [AI-Slop ransomware test sneaks on to VS Code marketplace - BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/ai-slop-ransomware-test-sneaks-on-to-vs-code-marketplace/)
- [Malicious VS Code AI Extensions With 1.5M Installs Found Exfiltrating Code - The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/01/malicious-vs-code-ai-extensions-with-15.html)
- [Fake Clawdbot VS Code Extension Installs ScreenConnect RAT - Aikido](https://www.aikido.dev/blog/fake-clawdbot-vscode-extension-malware)
- [Solidity Devs Targeted Again: Malicious VS Code Extension Drops ScreenConnect RAT - Checkmarx](https://checkmarx.com/zero-post/solidity-devs-targeted-again-malicious-vs-code-extension-drops-screenconnect-based-remote-access-trojan-rat/)
- [VS Code extensions contain trojan-laden image - ReversingLabs](https://www.reversinglabs.com/blog/malicious-vs-code-fake-image)
- [Malicious VSCode extensions on Microsoft's registry drop infostealers - BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/malicious-vscode-extensions-on-microsofts-registry-drop-infostealers/)
- [Malicious VSCode extensions infect Windows with cryptominers - BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/malicious-vscode-extensions-infect-windows-with-cryptominers/)
- [Nx Compromised to Steal Wallets and Credentials - Semgrep](https://semgrep.dev/blog/2025/security-alert-nx-compromised-to-steal-wallets-and-credentials)
- [Supply Chain Risk in VS Code Extension Marketplaces - Wiz](https://www.wiz.io/blog/supply-chain-risk-in-vscode-extension-marketplaces)
- [3,800 internal repos at GitHub breached via a malicious VS Code extension: why developer devices are the real target](https://www.aikido.dev/blog/github-breached-vs-code-extension)

Allow for `minimumReleaseAge`-style security config from other package managers / updaters, to require a minimum age on VS Code extensions before they are installed (also when installed via CLI, etc) when either:

1. Installing the latest version
2. Updating an extension manually
3. Updating an extension automatically

**Default:** Also, similar to the pnpm v11 note in Prior Art below, consider making a small delay the default (somewhere between 1 and 3 days), so that there is time for:

1. security scanners such as [Socket](https://socket.dev/) to find and report malicious extensions
2. VS Code Marketplace and OpenVSX to remove the malicious extensions

**Exclude mechanism:** There should be a way of excluding certain package names, package name patterns and publishers from the `minimumReleaseAge` setting, eg. like the pnpm [`minimumReleaseAgeExclude`](https://pnpm.io/settings#minimumreleaseageexclude) setting.

**Centralized management via enterprise policy:** Some users have commented that a centralized management via eg. GPO or MDM would be helpful:

> @SherwoodFold in [comment 4510110043](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/316867#issuecomment-4510110043): Additionally, this setting needs to be manageable by MDM profiles/configs so admins can actually manage their org's exposure.

@HendrikJan opened a similar issue https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/272765 which collected 12 upvotes. It was marked as a duplicate of https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/79689, but https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/79689 is not related to security (and is closed).

## Prior Art

- JavaScript / TypeScript package managers
  - [npm `min-release-age`](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/using-npm/config#min-release-age)
  - [Yarn `npmMinimalAgeGate`](https://yarnpkg.com/configuration/yarnrc#npmMinimalAgeGate)
  - [pnpm `minimumReleaseAge`](https://pnpm.io/settings#minimumreleaseage)
  - [Bun `minimumReleaseAge`](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/bunfig#install-minimumreleaseage)
  - [Deno `--minimum-dependency-age`](https://docs.deno.com/runtime/reference/cli/install/)
- CI update bots / update tools
  - [Dependabot `cooldown`](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#cooldown-)
  - [Renovate `minimumReleaseAge`](https://docs.renovatebot.com/key-concepts/minimum-release-age/)
  - [Snyk automatic dependency upgrade PR 21-day cooldown](https://docs.snyk.io/scan-with-snyk/pull-requests/snyk-pull-or-merge-requests/enable-automatic-upgrade-prs-for-new-dependency-upgrades#:~:text=Snyk%20does%20not%20recommend%20upgrades%20to%20versions%20that%20are%20less%20than%2021%20days%20old)
  - [npm-check-updates `--cooldown`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/npm-check-updates#cooldown)
- Other package managers
  - [pip `--uploaded-prior-to`](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/user_guide/#filtering-by-upload-time)
  - [uv `exclude-newer`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/settings/#exclude-newer)
  - [Haskell Cabal `--index-state`](https://cabal.readthedocs.io/en/stable/cabal-commands.html#cmdoption-index-state) (only absolute timestamps)
  - [R / Posit Package Manager snapshot identifiers](https://docs.posit.co/rspm/admin/repositories.html#snapshot-identifiers) (only absolute dates)

A lot of these have appeared lately because of the supply chain attacks over the last years.

**Default:** pnpm v11 recently changed the default to 1-day `minimumReleaseAge` without any configuration:

> Supply-chain protection on by default. [`minimumReleaseAge`](https://pnpm.io/settings#minimumreleaseage) defaults to 1440 (1 day)

Source: https://pnpm.io/blog/releases/11.0

title: [Chrome OS] Chinese IME not working with native Chrome OS IME (GTK_IM_MODULE=cros)
body:
**Issue Description**
Unable to input Chinese (Traditional Chinese) in VSCode on Chromebook. Input method switching has no effect and only English input is possible. All other applications including Linux terminal can input Chinese normally.

**Environment**
- **OS**: Chrome OS (Developer Mode enabled)
  - Kernel: Linux x64 6.6.99-09000-gd3ae1caecf39
- **VSCode Version**: 1.109.0
  - Commit: bdd88df003631aaa0bcbe057cb0a940b80a476fa
  - Date: 2026-02-04T02:01:38.288Z
  - Electron: 39.3.0
  - Chromium: 142.0.7444.265
- **Installation Method**: Official .deb package from VSCode website, installed via Linux (Crostini)
- **System Language**: Traditional Chinese (zh-TW)
- **Input Method**: Chrome OS native IME (Cros IME)

**Steps to Reproduce**
1. Set Chromebook system language to Traditional Chinese
2. Enable Developer Mode on Chromebook
3. Download VSCode .deb package from official website
4. Install via Crostini Linux container
5. Launch VSCode
6. Create new file or open existing file
7. Attempt to switch to Chinese input method
8. Try to type Chinese characters

**Expected Behavior**
- Input method should switch successfully
- Chinese characters should be inputtable with candidate selection window
- IME should work as it does in other Linux applications on Chrome OS

**Actual Behavior**
- Input method switching has **no effect** in VSCode
- Only English characters can be typed
- No candidate selection window appears
- Chinese input completely non-functional in VSCode **only**

**Additional Testing**
- ✅ Chinese input in Chrome browser: **Works normally**
- ✅ Chinese input in Linux Terminal: **Works normally** (tested with command input)
- ✅ Chinese input in other Linux apps: **Works normally**
- ❌ Chinese input in VSCode: **Does not work**

**System Configuration**

Input method framework check:
```bash
$ ps aux | grep -E 'fcitx|ibus'
# No fcitx or ibus running (using Chrome OS native IME)
```

Locale information:
```
LANG=en_US.UTF-8
LANGUAGE=
LC_CTYPE="en_US.UTF-8"
LC_NUMERIC="en_US.UTF-8"
LC_TIME="en_US.UTF-8"
LC_COLLATE="en_US.UTF-8"
LC_MONETARY="en_US.UTF-8"
LC_MESSAGES="en_US.UTF-8"
LC_PAPER="en_US.UTF-8"
LC_NAME="en_US.UTF-8"
LC_ADDRESS="en_US.UTF-8"
LC_TELEPHONE="en_US.UTF-8"
LC_MEASUREMENT="en_US.UTF-8"
LC_IDENTIFICATION="en_US.UTF-8"
LC_ALL=
```

Environment variables:
```
LANG: en_US.UTF-8
LC_ALL: 
XMODIFIERS: 
GTK_IM_MODULE: cros
QT_IM_MODULE: cros
```

**Root Cause Analysis**
The system is using Chrome OS's native input method module (`GTK_IM_MODULE: cros`), which works perfectly in all other Linux applications including the terminal. However, VSCode's Electron framework appears to be unable to communicate with the `cros` IME module.

This is **NOT** a general IME issue, as the same input method works flawlessly in:
- Chrome browser
- Linux terminal (tested: `中文輸入`)
- Other Linux applications

This appears to be specific to VSCode/Electron's integration with Chrome OS's native IME system.

**Workarounds Attempted**
- [x] Verified Chinese input works in other applications
- [x] Checked locale and environment variables
- [x] Confirmed GTK_IM_MODULE is set to 'cros'
- [ ] Installing fcitx/ibus (not ideal as Chrome OS native IME works everywhere else)

**Possible Solutions**
1. VSCode/Electron should properly support `GTK_IM_MODULE=cros` on Chrome OS
2. Add Chrome OS IME compatibility layer
3. Provide documentation for Chrome OS users on proper IME configuration

**Impact**
This affects all Chromebook users running VSCode in Crostini with non-Latin input methods (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, etc.). Given Chrome OS's popularity in education and enterprise, this is a significant accessibility issue.

**Related Issues**
- Potentially related to Electron's IME handling on Linux
- May be similar to other Chrome OS/Crostini IME issues

**Environment Variables for Reference**
For other Chrome OS users experiencing this issue, the working configuration in other apps is:
```bash
GTK_IM_MODULE=cros
QT_IM_MODULE=cros
```

title: Terminal command edits are silently ignored when using Claude Agent SDK (works correctly with regular Copilot)
body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.37.1
- VS Code Version: 1.109.0
- OS Version: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200 using WSL2 Ubuntu
- Feature: Claude Agent SDK integration
- Selected model: Claude Opus 4.5

Description
When an agent proposes a terminal command, VS Code shows a prompt allowing the user to edit the command before executing. This works correctly in regular Copilot sessions — the edited command runs and the agent receives the edited output. However, when using Claude Agent SDK as the agent provider, user edits to the proposed command are silently ignored: the original agent-proposed command runs regardless, and the agent never sees the user's changes.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open VS Code with Copilot extension (latest stable)
2. Switch to Claude Agent SDK as the agent provider
3. Start a task that causes the agent to run a terminal command (e.g., echo "Hello")
4. When the command approval prompt appears, edit the command (e.g., change to echo "Stop")
5. Click "Allow" to execute

Expected Behavior
- The edited command (echo "Stop") runs in the terminal
- The agent sees the edited command and its output
- Agent note appears: "Note: The user manually edited the command to echo 'Stop'..."
- This is how it works in regular Copilot sessions and is documented behavior that agents rely on for user steering.

Actual Behavior
- The original agent-proposed command (echo "Hello") runs instead
- User edits are silently discarded
- The agent has no awareness that the user attempted to modify the command

Real-World Impact
This is a significant workflow limitation. Users often edit terminal commands to:
- Steer the agent when it's about to do something slightly wrong
- Inject feedback mid-execution (e.g., editing echo "" to echo "stop, fix X first")
- Correct paths or flags before execution
Without this working, users lose a key interactive control mechanism and must wait for the agent to finish before providing feedback.

Concrete Example
During a multi-agent workflow, a subagent started reading irrelevant files. The user edited a terminal command to echo "End task" to signal the agent to stop. The edit was ignored — the original command ran, and the agent continued processing unrelated files, wasting context and tokens.

Notes
- Regular Copilot agent sessions handle command edits correctly
- This appears specific to the Claude Agent SDK integration path
- The edit UI prompt appears and accepts input, so the user believes their edit was applied

title: GitHub Copilot `grep_search` `includePattern` silently fails with workspace root folder name prefix in multi-root workspaces (severe)
body:
## Summary

In a multi-root workspace, GitHub Copilot's `grep_search`'s `includePattern` does not recognize the workspace root folder name as a path prefix. The pattern `rootname/path/to/file.ext` silently returns zero results with a misleading error message, even though `file_search` finds the same file with the identical pattern.

This is the single largest source of LLM search failures in multi-root workspaces. Two additional lower-severity bugs discovered during this investigation are filed separately (see §Related Issues).

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 11 (likely affects all platforms — see §Recommended Test Suite)
- **VS Code:** 1.109
- **Workspace:** Multi-root (3 roots)

## Reproduction

### Setup

Create a multi-root workspace with two roots:

```
C:\projects\alpha\       ← workspace root "alpha"
    src/
        hello.txt        ← contains "hello world"
C:\projects\beta\        ← workspace root "beta"
    src/
        hello.txt        ← contains "goodbye world"
```

### Steps

1. Open both folders as a multi-root workspace.
2. Use `grep_search` with `includePattern: "alpha/src/hello.txt"` and `query: "hello"`.
3. Use `file_search` with `query: "alpha/src/hello.txt"`.
4. Use `grep_search` with `includePattern: "src/hello.txt"` and `query: "hello"` (workaround).

### Expected

Steps 2 and 3 both find `C:\projects\alpha\src\hello.txt`.

### Actual

- **Step 2** (`grep_search`, root-prefixed): ❌ Returns no results. Error message: *"Your search pattern might be excluded completely by either the search.exclude settings or .\*ignore files."*
- **Step 3** (`file_search`, root-prefixed): ✅ Finds the file.
- **Step 4** (`grep_search`, root-relative): ✅ Finds the file — but matches _both_ roots, defeating the purpose of scoping.

## The Discrepancy

| `includePattern` / `query` | `file_search` | `grep_search` |
|---|---|---|
| `alpha/src/hello.txt` (root-prefixed) | ✅ | ❌ |
| `alpha/**/hello.txt` (root-prefixed glob) | ✅ | ❌ |
| `src/hello.txt` (root-relative) | ✅ | ✅ |
| `**/hello.txt` (recursive glob) | ✅ | ✅ |

The tools agree on root-relative and recursive patterns, but diverge on root-prefixed patterns. Slash direction (`/` vs. `\` vs. mixed) has no effect on this behavior — the results are identical in all slash variants.

## Why This Is Critical for LLMs

1. **Natural behavior leads to failure.** LLMs use `file_search` to locate files, get back results, and learn that `rootname/path` is valid. They then pass the same root-prefixed path to `grep_search` as `includePattern` — which silently returns nothing.

2. **The error message misdirects.** The LLM is told the file "might be excluded by `.gitignore` or `search.exclude`." This is false. The LLM then retries with `includeIgnoredFiles: true` (doesn't help), and may eventually fall back to terminal commands, bypassing VS Code's search infrastructure entirely.

3. **No way to scope `grep_search` to a specific root.** The only workaround is root-relative paths (e.g., `src/hello.txt`), which match files in _every_ root. In a multi-root workspace with similar directory structures, this produces unwanted cross-root results.

## Confounding Factor: False Positives with `**`

The root-prefixed `**` pattern (`alpha/**/hello.txt`) can _appear_ to succeed if the root folder name coincidentally matches a directory segment inside the file tree (e.g., `src/com/alpha/util/Hello.java` contains a directory named `alpha`). The `**` traverses to the coincidental match, not the root prefix. This creates false confidence in projects where the name coincidence exists, and silent failure in projects where it does not — making the bug appear intermittent when it is actually deterministic.

## Root Cause Hypothesis

`grep_search` appears to delegate to a VS Code API that resolves `includePattern` globs strictly against paths relative to each workspace root's content directory. `file_search` appears to use a different API that additionally accepts the root folder name as a scope prefix. The two APIs have different multi-root path resolution semantics, but this distinction is not surfaced in the tool documentation.

## Recommendation

1. `grep_search` `includePattern` should accept root folder names as path prefixes, consistent with `file_search`.
2. The error message when `includePattern` matches no files should not suggest `.gitignore` or `search.exclude` unless those are actually responsible.

## Related Issues

Two additional bugs discovered during this investigation:

- #293430 — `file_search` glob `\**\` (backslash double-star) produces partial or no results where `/**/` succeeds. Lower severity; only affects Windows backslash glob patterns.
- #293204 — Malformed absolute paths (`\c\path` or `/c/path`) trigger "Allow reading external files?" prompt, then fail. Affects `read_file` and `list_dir`.

## Recommended Test Suite

To prevent these discrepancies and catch regressions:

1. **Tool parity:** `grep_search` and `file_search` produce equivalent results for identical path patterns (root-relative, root-prefixed, recursive glob, explicit path).
2. **Multi-root scoping:** Root-prefixed paths correctly scope to the named root. Test with a root name that does _not_ appear as any internal directory segment to avoid false positives.
3. **Error message accuracy:** When `includePattern` produces no results due to an unrecognized path format, the message should not claim `.gitignore`/`search.exclude` exclusion.
4. **Platform coverage:** Run on Windows (cmd and Git Bash), macOS, and Linux.

title: Make .copilotignore apply to Workspace Tasks and Launch metadata
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
I've noticed an inconsistency in how .copilotignore handles workspace files.
When I add .vscode/tasks.json or .vscode/launch.json to .copilotignore, Copilot correctly stops reading the file contents. However, the parsed metadata (task names, commands, and arguments) is still fetched via VS Code APIs and sent to the LLM context in the <workspace_info> section.

Described Behavior:

User adds **/tasks.json to .copilotignore.

Copilot Chat still sends the task list (including command arguments) to the model to support task-running capabilities.

Why this is important:
Users typically expect that adding a file to .copilotignore means "Copilot should not know about this file or its contents."
The current behavior creates a gap where sensitive command arguments (even if not secrets, but internal logic) are shared unexpectedly.

Describe the solution you'd like
It would be great if the extension could check the .copilotignore rules before populating the <workspace_info> section.
If the source file of a Task or Launch Configuration is ignored, its metadata should also be excluded from the context sent to the server.

Alternative
If filtering metadata is technically difficult, a setting to opt-out of sending "Workspace Environment State" (Tasks/Terminal info) would be a helpful workaround for users who need stricter control over the context window.

Thank you!

title: WebView browser panel gets stuck and becomes unclosable after opening a new project
body: Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes - VS Code Version: 1.118.1 - OS Version: macOS Tahoe 26.1 (MacBook Air 13", Apple Silicon M4, 2025) ## Description While working on a React Vite project, I started using a new VS Code feature where clicking a `http://localhost:5173/` link in the terminal opens an embedded browser window inside VS Code (WebView). This feature works really well, especially the integration with GitHub Copilot, which allows sending HTML snippets or selecting parts of the UI for context. Observe that the WebView browser remains stuck on screen and cannot be closed

title: Copilot Chat Agent uses wrong session/file context when multiple chat sessions are active
body:
## Summary

I am seeing repeated context pollution between VS Code Copilot Chat Agent sessions. A follow-up prompt sent in one session can pick up the active file/context from another session and then edit the wrong file.

In this minimal repro, I created `page-01.html` in one session and `page-02.html` in another session. Then I sent a follow-up message, `Add footer.`, in the first session. The conversation history for that session was about `page-01.html`, but the request sent to the model included `editorContext` for `page-02.html`, and the agent edited `page-02.html` instead.

This looks related to hidden/stale `editorContext` taking precedence over the chat session's own history.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a workspace in VS Code.
2. Start Copilot Chat Agent session A.
3. In session A, ask: `Create page-01.html with dummy text.`
4. Start Copilot Chat Agent session B.
5. In session B, ask: `Create page-02.html with dummy text.`
6. In session B, send a follow-up prompt: `Add columns.`
7. Return to session A.
8. In session A, send a follow-up prompt: `Add footer.`

## Expected Behavior

The `Add footer.` follow-up in session A should use session A's conversation context and edit `page-01.html`.

If VS Code wants to include active editor context, it should either:

- show the attached file visibly in the chat input before sending, so the user can remove it; or
- avoid silently injecting active-file context when the chat session history points to a different file/task.

## Actual Behavior

The `Add footer.` follow-up in session A was sent with hidden `editorContext` pointing at `page-02.html`. The agent then read and edited `page-02.html`, even though the user was continuing the `page-01.html` session.

## Relevant Log Evidence

The `Add footer.` request shows the polluted editor context:

```text
<editorContext>
The user's current file is /Users/x/vs-code-sessions-test/page-02.html.
</editorContext>
...
<userRequest>
Add footer.
</userRequest>
```

The same request's previous conversation history is from the `page-01.html` session:

```text
<userRequest>
Create `page-01.html` with dummy text.
</userRequest>
...
create_file ... "filePath":"/Users/x/vs-code-sessions-test/page-01.html"
...
Created [page-01.html] ... with a minimal HTML skeleton and dummy text.
```

But after receiving `Add footer.`, the agent immediately reads `page-02.html`:

```json
{
  "tool": "read_file",
  "args": "{\"filePath\":\"/Users/x/vs-code-sessions-test/page-02.html\",\"startLine\":1,\"endLine\":200}"
}
```

Then the agent patches `page-02.html`:

```json
{
  "tool": "apply_patch",
  "args": "... Update File: /Users/x/vs-code-sessions-test/page-02.html ... <footer> ... Footer content goes here. ..."
}
```

It also validates the wrong file:

```json
{
  "tool": "run_in_terminal",
  "args": "... const p='/Users/x/vs-code-sessions-test/page-02.html'; ... console.log('footer present'); ..."
}
```

## Attached Logs

I can provide these logs from the repro:

- `logs/01__Create__page_01_html__with_dummy_text__logs.json`
- `logs/02__Create__page_02_html__with_dummy_text__logs.json`
- `logs/03__Add_columns__logs.json`
- `logs/04__Add_footer__logs.json`

The strongest evidence is in `logs/04__Add_footer__logs.json`, where the request includes the first session's previous `page-01.html` conversation but silently injects `editorContext` for `page-02.html`.

## Impact

This can cause Agent mode to modify the wrong file or project when multiple chat sessions are open. The user may believe they are continuing one session, while hidden active-editor context from another session changes the agent's target.

This is especially risky for short follow-up prompts such as `Add footer.`, `Continue.`, `Fix it.`, or `Add tests.`, where the intended target is defined by the current chat session history.

## Related Issues

This appears similar to these context/reference contamination reports:

- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/307867
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-copilot-release/issues/7361
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-copilot-release/issues/6393
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/305251
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/286950

## Environment

- VS Code Version: 1.119.0 Commit: 8b640eef5a6c6089c029249d48efa5c99adf7d51
- OS: macOS
- Mode: Copilot Chat Agent/Edit Agent
- Model in logs: `gpt-5.4-mini`
- Workspace: single test workspace with `page-01.html` and `page-02.html`

I can provide full debug logs if needed.

title: Agents window: corrupted session file silently loads as empty instead of surfacing error
body:
## Bug Description

When opening an old session in the Agents window, if the Copilot SDK rejects `session.resume` due to a validation error in the session file, the agent host silently falls back to `createSession` with the same ID. This results in the session appearing to load successfully but showing **0 turns** — all conversation history is lost without any user-facing error.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have an existing agent session with conversation history
2. The session file becomes corrupted (in this case, a compaction metadata field fails validation)
3. Open the session in the Agents window
4. Session appears empty — no error shown to user

## Expected Behavior

The user should be informed that the session could not be restored due to corruption, rather than silently presenting an empty session.

## Actual Behavior

The session loads with 0 turns. The user sees a blank conversation with no indication that data was lost.

## Relevant Logs

```
[Copilot:df7c418f-...] _resumeSession called — session not in memory, resuming...
[Copilot:df7c418f-...] Calling SDK resumeSession...
[Copilot:df7c418f-...] SDK resumeSession failed: code=-32603, message=Request session.resume failed with message: Session file is corrupted (line 19567: data.compactionTokensUsed.copilotUsage.tokenDetails.0.batchSize: Number must be greater than 0)
[Copilot:df7c418f-...] Resume failed (code=-32603), falling back to createSession with same ID
[Copilot:df7c418f-...] Fallback createSession succeeded
[AgentHostStateManager] Restored session: copilotcli:/df7c418f-... (0 turns)
[AgentService] Restored session copilotcli:/df7c418f-... with 0 turns
```

## Analysis

The fallback logic is in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts` around line 1626:

```typescript
if (!err || errCode !== -32603) {
    throw err;
}
// Falls back to createSession with same ID
```

The comment says _"The SDK fails to resume sessions that have no messages"_ — but error code `-32603` is also returned for **data corruption**, not just empty sessions. The fallback does not distinguish between these cases.

## Suggested Fix

Two potential approaches:
1. **Agent Host**: Parse the error message to distinguish "no messages" from "corrupted" — surface a notification to the user when data is actually corrupted rather than silently creating an empty session
2. **SDK**: The validation on `batchSize > 0` in compaction metadata should not prevent loading the actual conversation turns — this is metadata, not content

title: Copilot Chat blocks the extension host ~60–135s at startup
body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Related: microsoft/vscode#315405 (same CopilotCLIChatSessionContentProvider), microsoft/vscode#299718 (WSL symptom), microsoft/vscode#263015 (local Windows symptom). None capture the CLI-cold-start-blocks-the-ext-host root across platforms. -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.50.1
- VS Code Version: 1.122.1
- OS Version: Windows 11 (10.0.26200), Snapdragon X / ARM64 — reproduces on local Windows folders AND in Remote-WSL (Ubuntu 24.04, arm64)
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Extension activation / Copilot CLI session integration (Agent Sessions view). Occurs before any chat mode is used.
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): N/A — the hang is during activation, before a model is selected. Seat: Copilot for Business (`copilot_for_business_seat_multi_quota`).
- Logs:

  **Startup Performance — Copilot Chat ENABLED** (Finish Activate, ms):
  ```
  GitHub.copilot-chat                  72278   (event: onChatSession:claude-code)   [up to 137816 on slower runs]
  hashicorp.terraform                  69289   (normally ~200)
  ms-azuretools.vscode-azureterraform  67385
  github.vscode-github-actions         71880
  ```
  All unrelated eager extensions cluster at ~67–72s — they finish only when the host unblocks.

  **GitHub Copilot Chat output channel:**
  ```
  ConversationFeature: Waiting for copilot token or BYOK model to activate conversation feature
          (~67–110s gap, nothing logged)
  [CopilotCLI] MCP server started. Server URI: unix:/tmp/mcp-XXXX/mcp.sock#%2Fmcp
  [CopilotCLIChatSessionContentProvider] listSessions took 101644 ms     (61928 ms on another run)
  activationBlocker from 'languageModelAccess' took for 102912 ms
  activationBlocker from 'conversationFeature' took for 63576 ms
  Fetched model metadata in 112450 ms
  ```

  **Startup Performance — Copilot Chat DISABLED** (same machine/network/reload):
  ```
  workbench ready                      1994
  hashicorp.terraform                   201
  ms-azuretools.vscode-azureterraform    83
  github.vscode-github-actions         1666
  (GitHub.copilot-chat no longer activates)
  ```

  **Each component is fast in isolation** (so it is not a single slow request — it is an internal Copilot CLI IDE-mode init stall):
  ```
  copilot --version                                   0.65 s
  docker pull hashicorp/terraform-mcp-server (digest) 0.9 s   (daemon up, 29.5.2)
  https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/                  0.34 s  (HTTP 401)
  https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp                 0.08 s  (HTTP 405)
  api.github.com/user, github.com/login/oauth/*, vscode.dev/redirect   < 0.4 s
  IPv6 to all hosts                                   fails instantly (no slow fallback)
  ```

## Description

On every window reload, `GitHub.copilot-chat` blocks for ~60–135s during activation while the Copilot CLI session integration (`CopilotCLIChatSessionContentProvider` → `listSessions`, gated behind the `onChatSession:*` activation) cold-starts its MCP server. The extension host is starved during this window, so every other eager extension's `activate()` is dragged out to the same ~60–70s and the window shows "activating extensions" for over a minute. Disabling GitHub Copilot Chat returns startup to ~2s and the other extensions to <2s. Reproduces on both local Windows and Remote-WSL, so it is not remote/WSL-specific.

Workarounds that did NOT help (only fully disabling Copilot Chat works): `http.proxySupport: off`; `github.copilot.chat.cli.showExternalSessions: false` + `github.copilot.chat.cli.mcp.enabled: false`; `chat.agentSessionsViewLocation: disabled` (the CLI session provider still spawns); GitHub sign-out; `--disable-extensions`.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Sign in to GitHub Copilot (Business seat) in VS Code 1.122.1 with GitHub Copilot Chat 0.50.1 enabled.
2. Open a workspace (local Windows folder or Remote-WSL) and reload the window (Developer: Reload Window).
3. Observe the window stays on "activating extensions" ~60–135s; run Developer: Startup Performance and see `GitHub.copilot-chat` Finish Activate ~60–130s with `[CopilotCLIChatSessionContentProvider] listSessions took ~60000–100000 ms`, and unrelated eager extensions (terraform, github-actions) dragged to the same time.
4. Disable GitHub Copilot Chat, reload — startup drops to ~2s and the other extensions to <2s.

title: Extension host crash loop: EXC_BREAKPOINT on V8Worker thread during Maglev concurrent compilation (macOS arm64, VS Code 1.126+/Electron 42.2.0)
body:
[vscode-maglev-crash-minidumps.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29720635/vscode-maglev-crash-minidumps.zip)

 this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No — the trigger requires a
sustained extension-host JS workload (see Steps to Reproduce). However, the crash site is
entirely inside V8's background compiler; there are no extension frames on the crashing stack.

- VS Code Version: 1.126.0, 1.127.0, and 1.128.0-insider commit 86df0e5dc86a78298b5ffce1c6f6793ad79c3e93 (all reproduce; stock downloads, untouched)
- OS Version: macOS 15.x, Apple Silicon (arm64)
- Electron: 42.2.0, Node 22.x

## Summary

Under a sustained agent-style chat workload, the extension host process
(`Code Helper (Plugin)`) deterministically crashes with **exit code 5** after
2–8 minutes. The crash is an `EXC_BREAKPOINT` (V8 CHECK/trap, `brk #0`) on a
background **V8Worker** thread, at a byte-identical PC in every crash:

```
Electron Framework +0x8fa45c
```

We collected **9 Crashpad minidumps** across three VS Code versions (including
1.128.0-insider), two storage backends, an automated test harness *and* an
interactive developer session. All 8 stable-build dumps have a frame-for-frame
identical crash-thread stack (heatmap below), the Insiders dump shows the same
EXC_BREAKPOINT-in-Electron-Framework-background-thread signature (different raw
offsets, as Insiders ships a different Electron Framework build), and disabling
V8's Maglev compiler (`--js-flags=--no-maglev`) makes the crash disappear
entirely in an otherwise unchanged A/B.

**Conclusion: a V8 Maglev concurrent (background) compilation bug in
Electron 42.2.0 tripping an internal CHECK while compiling extension-host JS.**

## Dump heatmap (8/8 dumps, single failure path)

Symbolicated against stock Electron 42.2.0 breakpad symbols. VS Code ships a
patched Electron build, so some neighboring symbol names are approximate (*),
but the Maglev frames form the exact real nesting order of a concurrent Maglev
compile — not producible by symbol skew.

| Heat | Frame | Symbol |
|---|---|---|
| 8/8 | pc, lr | `+0x8fa45c` / `+0x8fa1fc` — CHECK/trap site (*) |
| 8/8 | frame[0] | `turboshaft::GraphEmitter<...>` (*) |
| 8/8 | frame[1] | `v8::internal::maglev::MaglevGraphBuilder::VisitSingleBytecode()` |
| 8/8 | frame[2] | (*) |
| 8/8 | frame[3] | `v8::internal::maglev::MaglevGraphBuilder::Build()` |
| 8/8 | frame[4,5] | `v8::internal::maglev::MaglevCompiler::Compile(LocalIsolate*, ...)` |
| 8/8 | frame[6,7] | `v8::internal::maglev::MaglevConcurrentDispatcher::JobTask::Run(v8::JobDelegate*)` |
| 8/8 | frame[8,9] | worker-pool thread bootstrap (*) |
| 8/8 | frame[10,11] | `libsystem_pthread` (`_pthread_start`) |

Zero variance across all 8 dumps: same PC, same LR, same 12-frame stack.

## The discriminating A/B: `--js-flags=--no-maglev`

Same machine, same day, same stock 1.127.0 binary, same test, same config:

| Run | `--js-flags=--no-maglev` | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| A | **yes** | **passed** — 1031 s sustained session, 45 chat turns, clean exit 0, peak ext-host RSS 405 MB |
| B (30 min later) | no | **crashed** — 334 s, exit code 5, minidump with the identical `+0x8fa45c` stack |

Two flagged runs survived a combined ~33 minutes of the workload that reliably
kills unflagged instances in 2–8 minutes.

## Ruled out

- **Native modules** — reproduced with the extension's only native module
  (`classic-level.node` / LevelDB) fully replaced by an in-memory Map.
- **Window reloads** — reproduced with reload cycles disabled.
- **Version-specific regression** — reproduces on 1.126.0, 1.127.0, and
  1.128.0-insider (commit 86df0e5d, 2026-07-06 build): extension host crashed
  with code 5 at t=344s (16 turns), t=99s (4 turns) on retry, and t=454s
  (13 turns) in a third run that captured a minidump (included in the
  attachment): EXC_BREAKPOINT, PC in `Electron Framework +0x6f72d8`, background
  (pthread) thread — same signature class; raw offsets differ because Insiders
  ships a different Electron Framework build.
- **Memory pressure / OOM** — ext-host RSS stays < ~500 MB throughout; crash
  is a CHECK trap, not `FatalProcessOutOfMemory`.
- **Extension/JS code** — crash thread is a V8 background compiler thread; no
  extension frames on the crashing stack.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install our extension (Augment) in stock VS Code 1.126.0, 1.127.0, or 1.128.0-insider on macOS arm64.
2. Run a long-lived AI-agent chat session in the extension host: repeated
   multi-turn streaming requests, large JSON message payloads, and periodic
   state persistence, sustained for up to 30 minutes.
3. The extension host (`Code Helper (Plugin)`) crashes with exit code 5 after
   2–8 minutes (149–480 s across runs in our automated Playwright harness).
4. Repeat with `--js-flags=--no-maglev` on the extension host (e.g. via
   `argv.json`): the identical workload runs to completion.

The workload requires our extension + backend, so it is not trivially
portable; we are happy to run the reproducer on request, capture additional
dumps, or test candidate fixes/flag combinations. The crashing stack itself
contains no extension frames.

## Crash log excerpt (renderer/main log)

```
Extension host with pid <N> exited with code: 5, signal: unknown.
[UtilityProcess type: extensionHost, pid: <N>]: crashed with code 5 and reason 'crashed'
```

Crashed thread name: `V8Worker`; exception: `EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)`.

## Workaround

`--js-flags=--no-maglev` on the extension-host process fully mitigates.

Verified end-user delivery path: adding `"js-flags": "--no-maglev"` to
`argv.json` propagates the flag to the extension-host utility process
(`Code Helper (Plugin)`, `--utility-sub-type=node.mojom.NodeService` — flag
visible on its command line), as well as renderer and other utility
processes. A stock instance without the argv.json entry does not carry the
flag (negative control).

## Attachments

- 9 Crashpad minidumps (`.dmp`): 8 from VS Code 1.126.0/1.127.0 and 1 from
  1.128.0-insider (`insiders-crash-52340899.dmp`, commit 86df0e5d)
- Symbolicated per-dump stacks (identical across the 8 stable dumps;
  representative one below)

```
pc        +0x8fa45c   (CHECK/trap site)
frame[1]  +0x2e481c   v8::internal::maglev::MaglevGraphBuilder::VisitSingleBytecode()
frame[3]  +0x35f45c   v8::internal::maglev::MaglevGraphBuilder::Build()
frame[4]  +0x7d4f4c   v8::internal::maglev::MaglevCompiler::Compile(...)
frame[5]  +0x7d4d2c   v8::internal::maglev::MaglevCompiler::Compile(...)
frame[6]  +0x4d9730   v8::internal::maglev::MaglevConcurrentDispatcher::JobTask::Run(...)
frame[7]  +0x4d92f8   v8::internal::maglev::MaglevConcurrentDispatcher::JobTask::Run(...)
frame[10] libsystem_pthread +0x6bc8
frame[11] libsystem_pthread +0x1b80   (_pthread_start)
```

Dump UUIDs: 1d1aa1cd, 25e67d29, 3debc2ad, 43f6e320, a9dc47d0, aa8d9657, af77f303, c6ed8c2b (stable); 52340899 (1.128.0-insider)

Insiders dump crash thread (raw offsets, Insiders Electron Framework build):

```
pc        Electron Framework +0x6f72d8   (EXC_BREAKPOINT / trap site)
lr        Electron Framework +0x6f7178
frames    Electron Framework +0x6f6fe8, +0x11cedf0, +0x72ea40, +0x86c1c8,
          +0x24571cc, +0x1413534, +0x251c158, +0xfebc9c
          libsystem_pthread +0x6bc8, +0x1b80 (_pthread_start)
```

title: Agents window: make model provider & billing clear for 3rd-party agents (Claude / Codex)
body:
### Summary
Offering Claude and Codex in the agent dropdown is currently ambiguous: users can't tell which model provider or subscription the harness runs against. This has been strong, recurring feedback, and I couldn't get a single user to understand the value prop and how it actually works without a lengthy explainer.

### Main blocker: Which provider/subscription is being used?
Most users assume that picking Claude runs against **their own Claude Code subscription**, and they'd love to keep using it inside our Agents UI. In reality the harness routes through the Copilot proxy and **counts against their GitHub Copilot tokens**.

**Impact:** Users don't realize this isn't their existing Claude Code subscription and instead consumes Copilot tokens — a serious trust risk once they find out.

### Model picker vs. agent picker
Developers use the same umbrella terms ("Claude", "Codex") for both **model families** and the **harness products**. The model picker and the agent picker don't differentiate their intent enough, so it's unclear what a selection actually means.

**Impact:** Users don't understand the agent picker and avoid using it.

### Prior art
The Claude tooltip in the **editor window** is a nice pattern worth building on.

### Ideas (not committed)
- Improve the labels and hover/tooltip details in the Agents window to explain the provider/subscription and billing.
- Extend the editor-window Claude tooltip to the **Codex** harness.
- Add equivalent tooltips in the **Agents window**.
- A one-off explainer the first time a user picks a 3rd-party agent.
- Make the active subscription explicit, with an easy toggle (e.g. disabling the Copilot proxy for Claude — foundation already started).

/cc @TylerLeonhardt @giuspepe

title: Agents window config refresh can terminate a newly resumed Copilot session
body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Built-in Agent Host using Copilot CLI 1.0.72
- VS Code Version: 1.131.0-insider (9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04)
- OS Version: macOS 26.5.2
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agents window, Agent Host Copilot session refresh
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): GPT-5.6 Sol
- Logs: Reproduced in Agent Host, AHP, persisted session events, and Copilot runtime logs. Sanitized causal timeline is included below.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Resume an existing `copilotcli` session in the Agents window.
2. Let the active client tool/plugin/MCP snapshot change structurally after the session was resumed, then send a message. This makes `ActiveClient.requiresRestart(...)` refresh the default chat.

The user-level repro is timing-dependent. A deterministic code-level repro is:

1. Hold the current SDK session's `disconnect()` promise open.
2. Register a structurally new client tool and send a message, forcing the config-refresh branch.
3. With the old code, observe that `_resumeSession()` starts before the held disconnect finishes.
4. Complete the old disconnect. Its `session.destroy` terminates the runtime session that was just resumed under the same session ID.
5. The turn fails with `Error: (query) Execution failed: Error: Holder terminated during creation`.

### Actual behavior

The turn fails before the first model response while the runtime builds settings and tools. Retrying in the same cached session fails again because the resumed session's shell-context holder is already terminal.

### Expected behavior

Refreshing a session after client configuration changes should fully tear down the previous runtime session before resuming the same session ID. The next message should run normally.

### Root cause analysis

The config-refresh branch in `CopilotAgent._sendMessage` called `clearDefaultChat()`. Disposing that chat disposes `CopilotSessionWrapper`, whose cleanup starts `session.disconnect()` without awaiting it. The code then immediately called `_resumeSession()` with the same SDK session ID.

The SDK's `disconnect()` sends `session.destroy` by session ID. Because teardown and resume were concurrent, the runtime completed `session.resume` first and processed the stale `session.destroy` afterward. Runtime session disposal calls shell shutdown, permanently terminating the shared `ShellContextHolder`. The resumed session object remained cached, but its next `buildSettingsAndTools` call could no longer create a shell context.

Observed UTC ordering:

- `13:00:11.523` — Agent Host detects `requiresRestart=true`, clears the cached default chat, and starts resume.
- `13:00:12.113` — Copilot runtime logs `Resumed session` for the same ID.
- `13:00:12.300` — Copilot runtime then logs `Closing session` for that ID.
- `13:00:12.348` — persisted events record `session.shutdown`.
- `13:00:12.350` — Copilot runtime logs `Destroyed session`.
- `13:00:19.238` — AHP emits `chat/error`: `Holder terminated during creation` from `getOrCreate` during `buildSettingsAndTools`.

The adjacent Notion authentication prompt and unrelated MCP startup failures are not causal.

### Proposed fix

Await `entry.destroySession()` before clearing the default chat and resuming the same SDK session ID. This keeps the old entry present until teardown completes, then disposes it and resumes. The wrapper's subsequent cleanup call to `disconnect()` is a no-op because the SDK session is already marked disconnected. Peer chats remain untouched.

title: Latest Node.js crashes when ran with --interpreted-frames-native-stack
body:
<!--
Thank you for reporting a possible bug in Node.js.

Please fill in as much of the template below as you can.

Version: output of `node -v`
Platform: output of `uname -a` (UNIX), or version and 32 or 64-bit (Windows)
Subsystem: if known, please specify the affected core module name

If possible, please provide code that demonstrates the problem, keeping it as
simple and free of external dependencies as you can.
-->

* **Version**: `master` / v12.0.0
* **Platform**: any
* **Subsystem**: V8

This is an upstream bug and there's already an [issue in the V8 tracker](https://bugs.chromium.org/p/v8/issues/detail?id=9122) as well as a [PR](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/v8/v8/+/1570582) to fix it, but since we're about to release v12.0.0 and the issue will be present there, I think it's a good idea to have this registered here in case users stumble upon that.

---

The `--interpreted-frames-native-stack` flag - which is used to allow system profilers to understand V8 interpreted frames - is not compatible with code cache, which we introduced a while back in https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/24950. If we try to run Node.js with this flag - regardless of the script being executed -, Node.js will crash:

```
$ ./node --interpreted-frames-native-stack
#
# Fatal error in , line 0
# Check failed: !obj->IsCode().
#
#
#
#FailureMessage Object: 0x7ffc8458e3a0[1]    16377 illegal hardware instruction (core dumped)  ./node --interpreted-frames-native-stack
```

We need to backport https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/v8/v8/+/1570582 once it lands upstream, as well as re-enable the Linux perf tests on our V8 CI machines (https://github.com/nodejs/build/issues/1774) once the flag is fixed.

title: Throw within queueMicrotask callbacks should not crash Node
body:
<!--
Thank you for reporting an issue.

This issue tracker is for bugs and issues found within Node.js core.
If you require more general support please file an issue on our help
repo. https://github.com/nodejs/help


Please fill in as much of the template below as you're able.

Version: output of `node -v`
Platform: output of `uname -a` (UNIX), or output of `"$([Environment]::OSVersion | ForEach-Object VersionString) $(if ([Environment]::Is64BitOperatingSystem) { "x64" } else { "x86" })"` in PowerShell console (Windows)
Subsystem: if known, please specify affected core module name
-->

* **Version**:v15.9.0
* **Platform**: macOS x86
* **Subsystem**: task_queues

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

```
λ node --trace-uncaught
Welcome to Node.js v15.9.0.
Type ".help" for more information.
> queueMicrotask(_ => { throw 1 });
undefined
>
node:internal/process/task_queues:94
    runMicrotasks();
    ^
1
Thrown at:
    at processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:94:5)
```

### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

Always.

### What is the expected behavior?

If I understood the [spec](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/timers-and-user-prompts.html#microtask-queuing) correct:

> The queueMicrotask(callback) method must queue a microtask to invoke callback, and if callback throws an exception, report the exception.

It should behave similarly as Timer tasks.

```
> setTimeout(_ => {throw 1});
Timeout {
  ...
}
> Uncaught 1
```


### What do you see instead?

Node crashed

### Additional information

I did some preliminary triages that hopefully helps a bit:

- `task_queues.js` invoke `runMicrotask`
- which is a JS binding from `node_task_queue.cc` which invokes V8's `PerformCheckpoint` under the hood.
- V8's `PerformCheckpoint` invoked V8's `RunMicrotasks` to actually evaluate those JS callbacks.

But since V8's `PerformCheckpoint` returns `void`. I'm not sure how can Node be aware of any exceptions threw during the evaluation of those JS callbacks. Chromium seems to handle this fine but I haven't got time looking at its source.

title: assert.ok: extremely slow error message generation for some code
body: ### Version v20.11.1 ### Platform Darwin wololobook 23.4.0 Darwin Kernel Version 23.4.0: Fri Mar 15 00:11:05 PDT 2024; root:xnu-10063.101.17~1/RELEASE_X86_64 x86_64 i386 Darwin ### Subsystem assert ### What steps will reproduce the bug? 1. Create an empty file with thousands of columns, e.g. 900,000 `;`'s 2. Append `require('node:assert')(null)` 3. `getErrMessage`, specifically `findColumn` feeding into `acorn` takes several minutes ### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition? We've experienced this in production a number of times but we were never able to figure out what the problem was. We ship minified code to AWS Lambda and utilize the `assert` module for, well, runtime assertions. We were seeing unexplainable timeouts whenever a falsy case was hit. It was luck that we found this in our test suite because we ran it through Terser by mistake. ### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior? I'd expect the column search to be much faster, closer to something in the sub second/milliseconds range. ### What do you see instead? It takes minutes to construct the assertion error message. It looks like a subset of the code may be passed to `acorn` (https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/lib/assert.js#L232) leading to syntax errors as it parses till the end (https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/lib/assert.js#L265), `acorn` then reports that error whenever it hits that point (https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/lib/assert.js#L278), `findColumn` then continues to the next token and reads more chunks if necessary and `acorn` starts from scratch. A bundler like Webpack emits an IIFE which itself contains an immediate block. I believe that is the majority of time spent for `acorn` traversing each token in it. I suspect the many errors come from that very block that is incomplete, so `acorn` wastes time trying to parse something that is known to be incomplete. ~I think a better regression to the reproduction section is to do an IIFE and drop semi colons in there: `(() => {;;;;;;;...;;;;;;require('node:assert')(null);})()`~. Interestingly enough, an IIFE around it is not affected by it. Another interesting thing is that this does not affect normal Error's - is there a particular reason why they run on two different implementations? ### Additional information

body:
### Version

v22.5.1

### Platform

```text
Linux linux 6.10.2-arch1-1 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sat, 27 Jul 2024 16:49:55 +0000 x86_64 GNU/Linux
```


### Subsystem

no modules were involved

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

Open Node.js interactive mode by typing `node` in the terminal.
2. Enter `while (false){}` or `while (false);`.
   - Notice the "undefined" display ready to be output.
3. Enter `while (true);` or `while (true){}`.
   - The terminal freezes and becomes unresponsive.


### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

It reproduces 100% of the time, the required condition is that you're on node.js interactive shell.

### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior?

the expected behavior would be the return value of the block of code used in the while-loop, since 'while (false);' returned `undefined`, something predictably consistent is also expected with 'while (true);'

### What do you see instead?

The terminal stops working until I kill the process manually with htop or `kill` command from another terminal.

### Additional information

the issue is that in node.js interactive mode, when I type "while (false){}" or "while (false);" it will make a vague display of undefined ready to be output, sort of like a google suggestion. Now, here's the real deal issue: try typing "while (true);" or "while (true){}" instead. Your terminal will freeze and the only way to stop node.js at that point would be to kill the process with kill or htop. I think I know the reason behind the issue: the "semi-google-suggestion-like" vague display. Its purpose is it show you what is ready to be displayed when you press Enter, to save you ease and time by assuming that you likely are just wanting to glance at outcomes oftentimes. But to achieve this process of simulating the google-like output display, it has to execute the command in the background, and wait for the return result of executing that command, then send it to the vague display, therefore resulting in the bug that freezes your terminal when you type "while (true);" in interactive mode.
